newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy second-quarter earnings fall.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy second-quarter earnings fall.

text.p: Minneapolis-based retailer Best Buy Co. Inc. reported lower second-quarter earnings Wednesday, reflecting higher costs associated with new stores and distribution facilities opened in the past year.
The seller of consumer electronics, appliances and home office equipment said earnings fell to $3.8 million, or 9 cents per share, from $5.7 million, or 13 cents per share, a year earlier.
The lower profits came despite a 24 percent gain in revenues for the second quarter ending Aug. 31 to $1.8 billion, with comparable store sales up 4 percent from the previous second quarter.

"Our comparable store sales results have benefited from an enhanced major appliance assortment and an increased emphasis on selling extended service plans," said Richard Schulze, chief exeuctive officer of Best Buy.
"Both initiatives helped to mitigate the effects of a continued promotional environment for personal computers and industry-wide softness in consumer electronics," he said.
Schultz said he believes these initiatives should result in improved operating results for the second half of fiscal 1997, compared with the prior year.

The company said it intends to open 10 new stores during its third fiscal quarter, which will include entry into the Tampa, Fla. market with four stores and into Memphis, Tenn. with one store. As of Aug. 31, the company operated 262 locations.
Best Buy's stock rose $1 to $22.625 in morning trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
